short: No national digital strategy is on record for Angola, only a public administration digitalisation agenda and a World Bank programme, so no stage is set.
gaps: evidence.csv holds no row for Angola on the national strategy; the systems listed (Agenda de Transição Digital da Administração Pública, a government-class agenda; PADA, a programme; the AI draft law, thematic) are noted classes and set no rung.

short: Burundi adopted a National Digital Policy in October 2026; no source found reports its text and period.
gaps: The Council of Ministers adopted the National Digital Policy on 14 October 2026, but no source gives its text, its period, a delivery plan or reporting. The 2020 World Bank statements of absence (BDI-001, BDI-002) are superseded.

short: Benin has a digital strategy to 2031 in preparation since February 2026, but no source found says whether it will be adopted or published.
gaps: No adopting act, public text, period, plan or reporting for the 2031 strategy; drafting began at the 5-6 February 2026 seminar and the 24 March 2026 statement still has it in preparation. The predecessor Digital strategy 2021-2026 (BEN-008 to BEN-012, ends 2026) is only announced, with no adopting act and no public text held, so it does not stand as an adopted strategy in force; its governance rows are not carried to the 2031 cell. Rung 3 needs adoption of a strategy and its public text.

short: Burkina Faso adopted a digital economy strategy in 2018, running to 2027, but no source found says whether its text is published.
gaps: No row says SN@DEN's text is published, so it stays at stage 2. Also held: the 'Feuille de route de transformation digitale 2030 (douze chantiers)', a national roadmap which every source calls only announced or presented, with no adopting act; it carries the body, reporting and last-twelve-months rows, and has no public text held. The rung above needs a public text for SN@DEN.

short: Botswana's cabinet adopted its digital transformation strategy in February 2020, running to 2026, but no source found says whether its text is published.
gaps: No row says the SmartBots text is published, and none gives a delivery plan or a progress report. The period (2021-2026) is from a third-party repository and ends this year; BWA-001 (23 September 2026) says the strategy and action plan will be formally launched in November 2026, which sits oddly beside the 2020 cabinet adoption and is not read as un-adopting it. BWA-047 (ESTDEV, 2020) says the strategy was created in 2020 and does not state adoption; it adds nothing to the rung. The rung above needs a public text.

short: The Central African Republic had a national digital plan in drafting in 2021, for 2020 to 2025, and no source says whether it was adopted.
gaps: Nothing after November 2021: no row says the plan was adopted, and its stated period (2020-2025) has ended. CAF-001 (2020) says there is no comprehensive digital strategy; the later drafting rows supersede it. The rung above needs a dated adoption and a public text. CAF-030 (June 2023) names a mandated agency but falls before the 36-month governance window, so governance stays empty.

short: Côte d'Ivoire has a published digital strategy for 2021-2025, now past its period; no source found says its 2025 successor has been adopted.
gaps: The Strategie nationale de transformation numerique 2025-2035 (successor) was validated in August 2025 but no adopting act is on record, so it cannot be staged above 2; its text is not shown public. The 2026-2028 ministry roadmap and the PND 2026-2030 are not national-class instruments. Reporting is claims of delivery (fibre km, services) measured against no stated target. No dated event inside the last twelve months.

short: Cameroon's 2016 digital plan has lapsed, and a new digital economy strategy was being finalised in October 2026; progress reports are not known.
gaps: The plan's own text gives 2016-2020 (CMR-006) while the ITU repository gives 2016-2025 (CMR-003); both end before 2026. The update of the plan (Strategie numerique du Cameroun) is at diagnostic stage awaiting government approval, with no text or period. No reporting against the plan has been found, and no finance fact falls inside the 36-month window.

short: DR Congo adopted a national digital plan in 2019, now past its period; no source found says its 2026 successor has been adopted.
gaps: Plan National du Numerique Horizon 2025 was validated at a 2019 workshop; no cabinet act is on record, and the ADN coordinator said in November 2023 that it was adopted in 2019 (COD-062). Its successors, the Politique sectorielle de l'economie numerique 2026-2030 (validated 4 Aug 2026, to go to the Council of Ministers; no action plan, steering body or monitoring yet) and the PNN2 2026-2030 (drafting or announced, costed, period 2026-2030), are not adopted. Reporting is a ministry estimate of 60% completion, not measured against targets. The two successors are not reconciled. A COMESA progress report of 1 Oct 2026 lists the launch of the 2026-2030 plan at USD 1 billion and names no adopting act or body.

short: Congo adopted Vision Congo Digital 2025 by decree in 2019; no source found reports its successor awaits approval, and its action plan and monitoring.
gaps: No row for a public text of Vision Congo Digital 2025; no action plan or monitoring shown, and no domestic budget line for it. The successor, Stratégie numérique 2030, is validated at ministry level but not adopted by decree (a January 2026 seminar speaks of still defining the strategy); its finance is donor (World Bank) only.

short: Comoros adopted a public, costed digital strategy to 2028 in 2018; no source found reports results against its targets.
gaps: No row for any published report on results against the strategy's targets, so rungs 4 and 5 are not reached; no domestic budget line tied to it; no dated event in the last twelve months. The adopting act is not named.

short: Cabo Verde approved a digital economy strategy to 2030 in 2024; no source found reports its public text, plan and reporting.
gaps: No row for a public text of the Estratégia para a Economia Digital 2025-2030, none for its plan, reporting, body or finance. Agenda Digital de Cabo Verde 2035 is in preparation (Resolução 72/2026 sets bases only; CPV-003 calls it approved, CPV-010 says it approves no strategy) and is not adopted; the 2019-2021 Agenda has ended.

short: Djibouti's cabinet heard a digital economy roadmap in March 2023; no source found says whether it was adopted.
gaps: Standing rests on a March 2023 communication to the Council of Ministers on the Djibouti Smart Nation roadmap for the digital economy (DJI-002), which records no adoption or approval. DJI-001 (7 Oct 2025) disagrees to the extent that it lists the elaboration of a national digital strategy as a challenge still open; both leave the country with no adopted strategy. No text, period, delivery plan, reporting or governance row has been found, and nothing dated inside the twelve months records a step forward.

short: Algeria adopted its national digital transformation strategy for 2025 to 2030 in May 2025, but no source found reports costs and results against its targets.
gaps: No adopting act is named (approval stated by El Chaab and the High Commissioner only). Reporting is activity throughout, measured against no strategy target, so stage 4 is not reached; the plan has actions with no cost (executive plan 2027-2030 in preparation); no domestic budget line is tied to the strategy (UNDP/Japan donor support only). Earlier DZA-050 and DZA-066 'drafting', DZA-061 'validated' and the 'announced' rows are superseded by the adoption rows; DZA-063 (Interior Ministry vision 2025-2030, May 2026) does not say adopted and is a ministry's presentation, so it sets nothing.

short: Egypt's Digital Egypt strategy, running from 2016, is listed as adopted in 2025, but no source found reports its text, plan and recent progress.
gaps: Adoption rests on the ITU repository's general listing (2025), with no adopting act, body or date, and no row shows the text public; no delivery plan, no domestic budget line, and reporting is activity only (EGY-005, Nov 2024). A second instrument, the National strategy for building a fully digital state, was announced for approval by the Supreme Council on 13 Mar 2024 with no approval recorded; it is not the instrument staged. Nothing on record in the last twelve months.

short: Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy, according to a June 2026 legal-status page; no source found says whether any is in preparation.
gaps: The only statement of absence is a third-party legal-status page (Levellers, reviewed 8 June 2026), not an Eritrean government source. Systems.csv holds only ministry-plan, thematic and sector-ict instruments (HSSDP III, IGIF action plan, ICT in Education policy, Communications Proclamation 1998), none a national digital strategy, so nothing stands in the way of stage 1 but nothing lifts it either.

short: Ethiopia's Council of Ministers approved Digital Ethiopia 2030, running to 2030, in November 2025, but no source found says whether its text is public.
gaps: No text: public row has been found for Digital Ethiopia 2030; the Ministry of Innovation and Technology gives it a five-year period to 2030 (ETH-025). The only public-text row (ETH-003) is for the predecessor Digital Ethiopia 2025 (period to 2025, ended; superseded 20 December 2025). No domestic finance line is tied to the 2030 strategy (ETH-002 is the predecessor's), and reporting is activity only, so stage 3 needs a public text and stage 4 needs published results.

short: Gabon's minister presented a national digitalisation strategy in April 2026 after the 2020-2025 plan ended; no source found says whether it has been adopted.
gaps: The strategy is known only from the minister's presentation of its main orientations on 3 April 2026 (GAB-063), which states no adoption or text; no period, delivery plan, reporting, body or finance row has been found for it, and its sector master plans are still to be drawn up. The predecessor, Plan national stratégique Gabon Digital 2025, ended in 2025 (GAB-002); its body and finance rows (GAB-003 to GAB-005) are not carried to the new instrument.

short: Ghana's Digital Economy Policy and Strategy was adopted in 2024 with a 2028 target; no source found says whether any progress report exists.
gaps: No progress report against the policy's own actions has been found, and no body is named as mandated. A research report dated 2025-10-08 (GHA-001) still calls the policy not final, but it rests on 2022 survey data and is dated only by publication, so it does not outweigh two 2024 rows saying approved and adopted. A successor, the National Digital Transformation and Emerging Technology Strategy, was only begun in April 2025 (GHA-010) and is not adopted. Stage 4 needs reporting published within three years, and the cap needs a mandated body and a domestic budget line.

short: Guinea's 2023-2027 digital strategy is public and costed, with a lead ministry named, but no source found says whether any progress report exists.
gaps: No implementation or results report has been found, so reporting is not established. Standing is read as adopted because the ministry published the text (version 1.2, 11 June 2024) and no source calls it a draft, but no adopting act is named; GIN-001 says validated and GIN-010 says its elaboration was still under way in December 2024. The period reads 2027 in the title and 2026 in one article (GIN-011). Also held: the 2016-2020 predecessor, ended, and a World Bank mention of a planned national digital economy policy and strategy (GIN-009) that names no document. Stage 4 needs published reporting within three years.

short: The Gambia's Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034 is published and reported adopted in 2024; no source found reports its delivery plan and any progress report.
gaps: The master plan has no governance, delivery-plan or reporting row of its own; the plan and finance rows (GMB-006, GMB-007) belong to the Digital ID and Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2028. That strategy is only validated (May 2024, GMB-004, GMB-013, GMB-015) with no accessible text (GMB-014), so it would stand at stage 2. Adoption of the master plan rests on a third-party report that names the government and Sept 2024 but no act; it is dated 2023-2033 in some sources. Stage 4 needs a costed or actioned plan and published reporting.

short: Guinea-Bissau adopted a 2025-2030 digital transformation strategy by decree in March 2025, with a public text, but no source found reports any report on results.
gaps: No published report against the strategy's targets has been found, so stage 4 is not reached; the plan states actions with dates but no cost. No mandated body is stated. Earlier statements that no national strategy existed (2022-2023, GNB-018 to GNB-020) and the January 2025 launch and drafting rows are superseded by the gazetted decree; a conflicting 2026-04 Fintech Times line (GNB-003) is a general remark that does not outweigh the decree.

short: Equatorial Guinea's national digital economy strategy was in drafting with World Bank support in September 2026; no source reports its adoption or a published text.
gaps: No adopting act, period, plan or reporting has been found, and no text is published; the strategy was still being completed and validated on 2026-09-02. The earlier ADIGE digital agenda (2019-2025, a ministry plan) has no evidence rows here; no body or finance is stated.

short: Kenya published a costed national digital master plan for 2022-2032, but no source found reports any published report against its targets.
gaps: No published report against the plan's targets has been found, so stage 4 is not reached. Body (ICT Authority, KEN-035, 2022) and donor finance (KEN-023, 2023-03-31) are dated before the 36-month window and are not carried; no domestic budget line is stated. No dated event in the last twelve months. The Digital Economy Blueprint 2019 (open period) is the predecessor.

short: Liberia has a National Digital Strategy 2025-2029, adopted per a March 2026 policy, with a costed plan, but no source reports results against its targets.
gaps: No progress report against the strategy's targets has been found, so stage 4 is not reached; no adopting act or date is named (adoption rests on the ministry's National Data Governance Policy saying Liberia 'has adopted' it, March 2026). Other national-class rows are the same instrument; the Digital Liberia ministry plan, Executive Order 163 and the NDMI are noted classes.

short: Libya's Prime Minister approved a government digital transformation strategy in April 2025, to 2030, but no source found reports its approved text.
gaps: The text held (LBY-007) is the December 2022 proposal, marked as a proposal on its cover; the strategy as approved in April 2025 is not held, and whether it differs is not established. No budget or mandated-body row has been found for the instrument, and no results report. The rows under the name National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030 (LBY-001, LBY-002, LBY-003) are the same strategy's later activity claims and an earlier drafting row. Stage 3 needs the approved text public.

short: Lesotho's digital transformation strategy to 2030 was approved in February 2025 and is published, but no source found reports its action plan and results.
gaps: No adopting act or date is named for the strategy (approval is the finance minister's statement of 19 February 2025 and a World Bank document). The strategy's text sets initiatives by priority with start windows counted from operationalisation, not calendar dates, and states no cost (LSO-039); the policy of the same year lists its detailed action plan as still to be developed (LSO-009), so the delivery plan is read conservatively as none. The text makes the Chief Digital Office accountable for the strategy and its monitoring (LSO-040); no finance row and no results report against its targets has been found, only a claim of implementation (LSO-001, LSO-042). The 2027/28 Budget Strategy Paper of 15 October 2026 commits government to fast-track the strategy (LSO-041) but states no finance line or results. The National Digital Policy 2024-2035 (LSO-004 to LSO-007, LSO-010) is a second adopted national instrument, also stage 3; the strategy is the newer adoption and the one the study names.

short: Morocco has Maroc Digital 2030, listed as adopted in 2025, with MAD 11 billion for 2024 to 2026, but no source reports a public text.
gaps: No row holds the Maroc Digital 2030 text as public, and the ITU listing names no adopting act or date; other rows call it launched or announced. Predecessor Maroc Numeric 2013 / Maroc Digital 2020 (ended 2020) and the 2020 ADD orientations note (to 2025) are not in force. Stage 3 needs a public text; reporting is only activity (MAR-004), so stage 4 is further off.

short: Madagascar has the Plan Stratégique Numérique 2023-2028, presented in 2024 with a USD 800 million estimate, but no source reports its adoption and public text.
gaps: No source uses adopted, approved, enacted or gazetted for the Plan Strategique Numerique 2023-2028, and no row holds its text as public; no reporting against it. A separate national digital roadmap (announced, from the Digital Readiness Assessment) is only prospective. The cost figure is the ministry's 2023-2024 estimate; later sources state none. Stage 3 needs a source's word of adoption and a public text.

short: Mali has a digital economy policy validated in 2024 with an action plan to 2029, but no source found reports its adoption.
gaps: PNDEN was validated at a workshop on 24 October 2024 and no source states adoption; no public text row. Periods conflict: 2021-2034 (MLI-007), action plan 2025-2029 (MLI-010), 2024-2028 (MLI-013, earlier). Predecessor Mali Numerique 2020 (ended 2020; draft-marked text, 27.30% execution rate) is not in force. Stage 3 needs adoption and a public text.

short: In 2019 Mozambique approved a national information society plan running to 2028, but no source found reports its delivery plan and published results.
gaps: No delivery plan is stated for this instrument in the rows (its Plano Operacional is approved with it but no row gives actions or cost), and no published report against its targets has been found; one older INTIC report (MOZ-031) gives its period as 2019-2023 against 2019-2028 in the resolution. The National Digital Transformation Strategy is still in drafting (launched 12 Feb 2026, its operational plan not costed, work deprioritised by the World Bank in 2025-26) and would replace it.

short: Mauritania approved a costed national digital agenda for 2022 to 2025 that has now ended; no source found reports results against its targets.
gaps: The ministry of digital transformation, created in 2021, is described in August 2025 as the institutional lever for the agenda (MRT-050), and the state digital agency presented its role in implementing the state's digital strategy in October 2026 (MRT-049); funding is donor-backed with no domestic budget line. No report against the agenda's own targets has been found, only claims of activity. The agenda was under evaluation and update in August 2025 (MRT-051); its successor, Agenda National de la Transformation Numerique 2030, was opened for preparation on 4 Dec 2025 (a consultant was contracted in July 2025) and has no adoption or text.

short: Mauritius launched a national digital transformation blueprint for 2025 to 2029 in 2025; no source found reports its cost or results against targets.
gaps: No source names an adopting act; adoption is read from the published text with no source calling it a draft, and from the presidential launch of 26 May 2025. The plan states no cost, and reporting is claims of activity (about 84 projects) measured against no target, so stage 4 is out of reach. One launch-day report (MUS-013) said the content was not yet unveiled; the full text was published on the MITCI site the next day. The earlier Digital Mauritius 2030 Strategic Plan (2018, to 2030) is also on record and is superseded by the Blueprint.

short: Malawi has a National Digitalization Policy for 2023 to 2028, approved by Cabinet, but no source found says whether its text is public.
gaps: No row says the National Digitalization Policy text is public, and its scope is not described by any source. A National Digital Economy Strategy 2023-2028 is also held (adopted per MWI-025, awaiting Cabinet in MWI-028; may be the same document). A National Digital Transformation Strategy is in validation (draft, February 2026; MWI-004, 006, 008) with a proposed council and donor finance only. No delivery plan or reporting on record.

short: Namibia launched its National Digital Strategy 2025-2029 in August 2025 with a public text; no source found reports any delivery plan or progress report.
gaps: No source names an adopting act or body; adopted rests on the published text (mict.gov.na, NAM-007) that no source calls a draft. Period is 2025-2029 in most rows and 2025-2028 in NAM-006, 013-016. No delivery plan, cost or progress report on record, and no finance row; a domestic budget line is also missing. No other national instrument held.

short: Niger's digital development policy for 2026 to 2035 was validated in March 2026 and awaits an approving decree; no source found reports its text.
gaps: The Politique nationale de developpement du numerique 2026-2035 is complete but awaiting its approving decree (June 2026); no adoption on record and no text row. The earlier Politique nationale du numerique 2021-2030 was drafted in 2020 and never adopted (NER-014 says no policy in March 2025). Stage 3 needs adoption and a public text. No cost, reporting, body or finance rows.

short: Nigeria has a ten-year digital economy strategy unveiled in 2019, but no source found reports results against its targets and its funding.
gaps: Reporting is activity only (statements of progress, no results against the strategy's targets), so stage 4 is out of reach; the plan states no cost, and no finance fact falls inside the 36 months. A 2025 repository gives the time frame as '2020 - ongoing' against the stated 2030 end, not a conflict for the rung. No other national instrument has been found.

short: Rwanda's Smart Rwanda plan, issued in 2015, ended in 2020, and a successor was in preparation in 2023, but no source reports its current status.
gaps: No text-public row for the Smart Rwanda 2020 Master Plan and no plan or reporting row. The Digital Transformation Strategy for Rwanda (ICT Master Plan 2021-2025) is held by one row (RWA-001) giving only its period, ended before 2026; nothing shows it adopted, and nothing on its text or reporting. Whether Smart Rwanda Master Plan II (drafting, 2023-10) succeeds that plan is not stated; no later row on its status.

short: Sudan's digital transformation ministry announced a strategy in 2025, but no source found says whether it was adopted or its text published.
gaps: One row: a 2026 bank tender refers to a strategy announced by the digital transformation ministry in 2025; no adopting act, text, period, plan, reporting or governance fact has been found. Adoption and a public text are what stand in the way of stage 3.

short: Senegal launched its New Deal Technologique for 2025 to 2034 and published the text, but no source says whether results are measured against its targets.
gaps: No source names an adopting act; adoption rests on the government's own published text (presidence.sn), which no source calls a draft. Reporting is activity only (first-year achievements, SEN-024, SEN-030), measured against no targets; the only execution rates (SEN-062) belong to the predecessor Stratégie Sénégal Numérique 2025 (period to 2025, replaced by the New Deal, so not a successor in preparation). The body (PM-chaired GouvNum) has no named act.

short: Sierra Leone approved its National Digital Development Policy in 2021 and publishes the text, but no source found says who approved it.
gaps: No act or body is named for the approval (SLE-002 says 'approved' in 2021; the policy text itself, SLE-011, only recommends approval). Governance facts for the policy (SLE-014 body:none, SLE-015 finance:not-stated) are dated 2021, outside the 36 months, so governance is empty; nothing dated in the last twelve months. Other national instruments held: National Innovation and Digital Strategy 2019-2029 (public text, standing only launched; also stage 3, older), National Digital Development Strategy 2022 (validated/drafting, no adoption or public-text row) and a draft National Digital Transformation Roadmap. Stage 4 needs a delivery plan and published results; the policy has neither.

short: Somalia launched a Digital Transformation Strategy for 2025 to 2030 after a consultation in October 2025, but no source found says whether it was adopted.
gaps: No source reports adoption of the Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2030: it was validated in consultation on 12-13 October 2025 (SOM-004, SOM-006) and then said to be 'launched' by the government on 16 October 2025 (SOM-002) with no adopting act or body named. The Council of Ministers approved a separate Inclusive Digital Policy on 23 January 2025 (SOM-010), but no period or text is given for it and it is not the strategy, so it sets nothing here. No text has been found or linked, so no public-text row exists. No governance, delivery plan, reporting or last-twelve-months fact has been found.

short: South Sudan was still developing its digital road map and master plan in June 2024; no source found says whether it has been adopted.
gaps: No adopting act, body, text, period, plan or reporting held; the last dated row is June 2024 and says the Road Map/Master Plan was still being developed. Rung 3 needs adoption and a public text. A 'South Sudan Digital Transformation Strategy' and a 'Digital Government Strategy' appear in systems.csv with no evidence rows.

short: The government of São Tomé and Príncipe had launched a national digital transformation strategy by March 2026; no source reports its adoption, text and period.
gaps: The government 'has launched' the strategy per a World Bank document of 2026-03-11, with no title, act, date, body, text, period, plan or reporting; a launch alone is announced, not adopted. Rung 3 needs adoption and a public text. The 2020 Estrategia Nacional para a Governacao Digital (approved by Resolucao 35/2020, period 2020/2024) is class government, noted and not assessed.

short: Eswatini has a 2024-2028 digital strategy named in sources, but no source found reports its standing, text and plan, so no stage is set.
gaps: evidence.csv holds no row for this country. systems.csv names an Eswatini Digitalisation Strategy (2024-2028, 'Government in Your Hand') and a Digital Transformation Roadmap in procurement, with no evidence rows setting standing, text, period, plan or reporting.

short: Seychelles validated a 2026-2031 digital and AI strategy in July 2026; no source found reports its adoption and text.
gaps: The National Digital & AI Strategy 2026-2031 completed its national validation workshop by July 2026; no adoption, public text, delivery plan or reporting has been found, and finance is not stated.

short: Chad has a 2020 to 2030 digital transformation strategy, but no source found reports its adoption and public text, so no stage is set.
gaps: No row on this instrument says it was approved, adopted, launched or drafted; sources only name it as existing, with period 2020-2030, and text public is not stated, so standing is not established. The World Bank (2023) both cites the strategy and says there is no comprehensive national digital strategy (TCD-003), and recommends adopting 'Chad Digital Strategy Horizon 2030' (TCD-004, drafting), which may be the same document but is a different named instrument. Tchad Connexion 2030 (national development plan and economic strategy) is also held. Needed for stage 3: a source word of adoption and a public text; no reporting row.

short: Togo's president said in 2022 the Togo Digital 2025 strategy was adopted, but no source reports its text and its 2025 to 2030 successor's progress.
gaps: No public text has been found for Togo Digital 2025, no delivery plan row, and reporting is activity counts only. Governance rows (2021) are outside the 36-month window and nothing is dated in the last twelve months. Successor Togo Digital 2025-2030 is only at consultant recruitment (May 2025, TGO-011/012/013) with no later row; a Global Fund audit (TGO-002, 2025-06-04) reports no coordinated national strategy, which does not outweigh the President's dated word of adoption.

short: Tunisia's National Digital Strategy 2021-2025 ended in 2025 and no named successor has been found, so no stage is set.
gaps: Stratégie nationale du numérique 2021-2025 ended in 2025 and no successor strategy is on record: TUN-001 gives only a 'broader national vision for 2026-2030', not a named strategy in preparation. The rows for the predecessor Tunisie Digitale 2020 (extended to 2025), including its 2018 targets, results table and governance chart (TUN-035 to TUN-038) and its body row (TUN-008), are not carried to this instrument; that plan has ended too, and its results were published in 2018, outside any window. No text, plan or governance rows for the 2021-2025 strategy.

short: Tanzania's Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034 was launched in 2024 and is public; no source found reports its cost and any report on its targets.
gaps: No finance line tied to the framework; no published report against its targets (TZA-011 is activity only); plan states dated targets with no cost. A World Bank March 2023 row (TZA-022) calls the then-current strategy a draft, superseded by the 2024 launch.

short: Uganda published its Vision for a Digital Uganda 2040 in 2022 with a costed plan; no source found reports any report on progress.
gaps: No reporting row for the Vision, and its governance rows (2022-09, UGA-019, UGA-020) fall outside the 36-month window. Also holds rows for the Digital Transformation Roadmap 2023/24-2027/28 (newer, launched 2023 by the Ministry/Government, source verbs 'developed' and 'launched', no adopting act and no public text on record, so announced only); an adoption act or published roadmap text would make it the instrument in force. The Vision's adoption rests on the read-as-adopted rule, with no approval act named.

short: South Africa has a final draft digital masterplan dated 2021, not public, with its 2020-2025 period ended; no source found reports its adoption.
gaps: No row says the Masterplan was approved or adopted; the only text held is the February 2021 final draft, and Economist Impact (2023) says the final version is not public. Its 2020-2025 period has ended. A Digital Economy Framework and Strategy (ZAF-004, 2023, drafting, to go to Cabinet) is the possible successor, with nothing newer. Stage 3 needs adoption, a public text and a period not ended. No governance facts held.

short: Zambia adopted a public national digital transformation strategy in 2023, running to 2027, with no cost stated; no source found reports progress against its targets.
gaps: No report on progress against the strategy's targets has been found, so reporting is empty. The delivery plan states no cost. ZMB-005 and ZMB-007 say only 'formulated' (announced) and are outranked by ZMB-002, which says 'was adopted' without naming an act. Also on record: the National Electronic Government Plan 2023-2026 (government class, not assessed). No change on record in the last twelve months.

short: Zimbabwe's Smart Zimbabwe 2030 Master Plan was launched in 2024 and runs to 2030; no delivery plan or results are known.
gaps: No delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and no results against the Master Plan's targets, have been found. The National Digital Roadmap 2026-2030 is being formulated (ZWE-001) and is not yet adopted. The body the Master Plan mandates is dated 2019, outside the 36-month window.
